items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: See how I got to know Coltrane personally, I had met him in the fifties but I had really got to know him because I lived at this house... Coltrane and I used to go out to Coltrane’s house and hang out with him. I knew him man, I knew this guy.

ctx.x: How can you foster that ability to invent melodies and what happened to you with this — being thrown in that situation? How can we do that now?

They’ve got to learn tunes. The more songs that you know that have melodic content — the brain is like a computer. You have to — if you put garbage in you’re going to get garbage out. So you have to put something up there. And one of the things that I always stress to my students when they’re in the workshops and things I do, how many melodies do you know? I’ve done artists-in-residencies in different places. I will never forget one time I was at the University of Utah. I asked the young people what do they want…
have to learn tunes. They’re learning too many things like exercises that take you through the two-five-one progression. Or I’m going to play the Dorian or the Lydiot or Idiot scale.
